candidate_relations.reason: Intravascular fibrinoid material is the histopathologic finding of cryoglobulin/fibrin thrombi, not the clinicopathologic diagnosis.
Hyperviscosity syndrome can accompany a 16% cryocrit and paraprotein but is not type I cryoglobulinemia with myeloma.
Cholesterol embolization syndrome is a retiform-purpura differential, not supported by cryoglobulin thrombi and lytic myeloma.
Cryoglobulinemic vasculitis usually denotes mixed immune-complex vasculitis, incompatible with type I myeloma-associated pauci-inflammatory occlusion.
